findings.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` instead of `||`, denying team admins
`teamId ?? 0` fallback makes the permission check meaningless for non-team bookings
Blacklist comparison lowercases the configured list but not the submitted guest email, allowing `Blocked@Example.com` to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
`uniqueGuests` does not dedupe the input array itself, so duplicate submitted emails create duplicate attendee rows via createMany
Server schema addGuests.schema.ts lacks the uniqueness refinement applied client-side, so it is not enforced for direct API calls
`sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, sending wrong 'scheduled' invite emails to pre-existing attendees and classifying blacklisted addresses as new guests
organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without optional access or fallback, throwing when the attendee list is empty
MultiEmail.tsx keys list items by array index despite mid-list removal, causing React to reuse wrong DOM nodes and display stale values
Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests, with no check that the booking is not cancelled/rejected or in the past
`isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is never cleared on edit or successful submit, leaving stale validation errors visible
Error message template string in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is always non-empty, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing raw `undefined: ...` codes
Single empty input produces `[""]` which skips the early return and shows a misleading uniqueness/validity error instead of a required state; an empty array silently no-ops with no feedback
Email failures are swallowed with `console.log` without logging the error object, making delivery failures undiagnosable
When all submitted guests are filtered out as blacklisted, the returned error is `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, misdescribing the cause
No tests for the new tRPC handler, permission logic, blacklist filtering, or the MultiEmail component

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `teamId ?? 0` fallback makes the permission check meaningless for non-team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission gate is `isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee`. The `teamId ?? 0` fallback only affects the *team-based* branch: for non-team bookings (`teamId` undefined), it will call `isTeamAdmin(user.id, 0)` and `isTeamOwner(user.id, 0)`, which will (in any typical implementation) evaluate to false, leaving permissions to be determined by `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee`. Nothing in the diff shows that passing `0` would incorrectly grant access or make the overall permission check “meaningless” for non-team bookings; it more likely just means “no team permissions apply.” Therefore the proposed finding is not a verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema addGuests.schema.ts lacks the uniqueness refinement applied client-side, so it is not enforced for direct API calls

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows client-side uniqueness validation in `AddGuestsDialog` via `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` to ensure emails are unique. However, the server-side input schema `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the submitted `guests` array itself. Therefore, a direct API call can submit duplicate emails that pass schema validation and reach `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendees or triggering a DB constraint error (depending on schema). This makes the finding a real, verifiable gap introduced/present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, sending wrong 'scheduled' invite emails to pre-existing attendees and classifying blacklisted addresses as new guests
organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without optional access or fallback, throwing when the attendee list is empty

adjudication.rationale: The new organizer email template does use `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without a guard. However, in the only new call site added in this diff (`addGuestsHandler`), the `CalendarEvent` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` is constructed from `bookingAttendees.attendees` after a successful `createMany` of `uniqueGuests`, and the handler throws if `uniqueGuests.length === 0`. That means `evt.attendees` should be non-empty in this flow (at minimum it includes the newly added guest records), so the proposed “attendee list is empty” crash is not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff, only a speculative edge case if `sendAddGuestsEmails` were called elsewhere with an empty attendee list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx keys list items by array index despite mid-list removal, causing React to reuse wrong DOM nodes and display stale values

adjudication.rationale: In `MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)` and also supports removing an arbitrary item via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using the array index as the React key in a list where items can be removed from the middle is a known correctness problem: after a removal, subsequent items shift indices, so React will reuse component/DOM instances for different emails, potentially preserving internal component state (e.g., focus, validation state inside `EmailField`) for the wrong row. This is a real issue introduced by the diff (the new `MultiEmail` component).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests, with no check that the booking is not cancelled/rejected or in the past

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...);` and the request is allowed if `isAttendee` is true). After that, the handler proceeds to update the booking attendees and send emails without checking any booking lifecycle constraints (no check for booking status such as cancelled/rejected, and no check that `booking.startTime`/`endTime` is in the future). The booking object includes `startTime`/`endTime` but they are only used to build the CalendarEvent, not to gate the mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is never cleared on edit or successful submit, leaving stale validation errors visible

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared when the user edits the email inputs (MultiEmail `onChange` doesn’t touch it), so the error message can remain visible even after fixing the emails. It’s also not cleared in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but leaves `isInvalidEmail` unchanged), so if the dialog is reopened after a previous validation failure, the stale error will still display because the component stays mounted with `open={isOpenDialog}` toggling visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message template string in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is always non-empty, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing raw `undefined: ...` codes

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `message` via a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always produces a (truthy) string, even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (resulting in e.g. `"undefined: <translated>"` or `"undefined: "`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback, and it can indeed surface a raw `undefined:` prefix to users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single empty input produces `[""]` which skips the early return and shows a misleading uniqueness/validity error instead of a required state; an empty array silently no-ops with no feedback
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that having a single empty input results in an array like [""] which bypasses expected empty/required handling and triggers misleading validation/uniqueness errors. This is the same underlying concern as the golden comment about starting state [""] causing validation issues and preferring an empty array with explicit empty-state handling in the component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failures are swallowed with `console.log` without logging the error object, making delivery failures undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` is wrapped in a `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log `err` (nor rethrow). This makes email delivery failures effectively silent/undiagnosable from logs, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When all submitted guests are filtered out as blacklisted, the returned error is `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, misdescribing the cause

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, guest emails are filtered into `uniqueGuests` by excluding (a) emails already in `booking.attendees` and (b) emails in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If all provided guests are blacklisted (or otherwise filtered out), `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and the handler throws `new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That message is also used for invalid/duplicate emails, so in the specific case where all guests are filtered out due to blacklist, the returned error misdescribes the actual cause.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for the new tRPC handler, permission logic, blacklist filtering, or the MultiEmail component

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality (UI component, dialog, tRPC schema/handler, and email templates) but does not add or modify any test files. While that absence is verifiable, it’s a process/coverage suggestion rather than a concrete defect (bug/security/correctness issue) demonstrably introduced by the diff itself, and the diff alone doesn’t establish a requirement that tests must be added here.
